THIS WRIT PETITION (CIVIL) HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 19.06.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 WP(C) NO. 22426 OF 2025 2  2025:KER:43679  JUDGMENT Dated this the 19th day of June, 2025
The writ petition is filed to quash Exts.P6 to P8 notices issued by the 2nd respondent.
2. The mother of the 1st petitioner is in possession of 1.44 Ares of land comprised in Re-survey No.182/9 in the 1st respondent Panchayat.
The mother of the 1st petitioner and the 2nd petitioner have entered into an agreement of lease, whereby the 2nd petitioner is running a tea stall in the above property.
Now, the 2nd respondent has issued Ext.P6 notice to the 1 st petitioner, alleging that he is running an unauthorised commercial activity and to stop the activity.
Even though the 2nd petitioner applied for a licence, the same has been rejected by the 2nd respondent.

Subsequently,
Ext.P7 notice has again been issued to the 1 st petitioner, to demolish the construction. The 1st respondent has also affixed Ext.P8 notice on the tea stall of the 2 nd petitioner, 2025:KER:43679 threatening to demolish the unauthorised construction.
Exts.P6 to P8 notices are illegal and arbitrary.
Hence, the writ petition.

3. Heard; the learned Counsel for the petitioners and the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the respondents.
4.
Indisputably, Exts.P6 to P8 notices are issued by the 2nd respondent invoking his powers under the Kerala Panchayat Building Rules, 2019.

5. Exts.P6 to P8 notices issued by the 2 nd respondent are appelable under Rule 108 of the Kerala Panchayat Building Rules, 2019, before the Tribunal for the Local Self Government Institutions (in short 'Tribunal').
6.
In light of the alternative statutory remedy, I am not inclined to entertain this writ petition.

In the aforesaid circumstances, I dismiss the writ petition, by reserving the right of the petitioners to challenge Exts.P6 to P8 notices before the Tribunal by 2025:KER:43679 filing an appeal, with a delay petition and stay petition, if necessary, within four weeks from today.

If such appeal is filed along with the above petitions, within the prescribed time period, the Tribunal shall consider the appeal, the stay petition and the delay petition, in accordance with law and on their merits, as expeditiously as possible.

Until such time orders are passed on the stay petition, if the appeal is filed Shibin Stanly vs Kadinamkulam Grama Panchayath, ... on 19 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126538474/
2 within the prescribed time period, the implementation of Exts.P6 to P8 shall stand deferred.
